name: Infrastructure Setup to support Real Estate initiatives (new site setup, relocation and closure)
impact: These initiatives are essential to ensure business continuity and support future growth. They address either the need to vacate existing Philips facilities or provide additional capacity for expanding teams. Delays or non-execution could lead to operational disruption, space constraints affecting productivity, higher costs, compliance risks related to lease obligations, and limitations on business expansion.
problem: Mandatory office exits and business growth are creating a critical need for workspace relocation and expansion. Failure to execute these initiatives on time could impact business continuity, employee productivity, growth plans, and compliance with facility exit commitments.
scope: This demand covers Infrastructure Services activities required to support the global Real Estate portfolio, including new site openings, office relocations, site consolidations, expansions, and site closures. Scope includes campus networking (Cisco/Juniper LAN), WAN connectivity, NAC, micro-segmentation, wireless infrastructure, collaboration and meeting room technologies, AV/display equipment, equipment room setup, and associated implementation services. Infrastructure requirements are directly driven by Real Estate projects and must be delivered before site occupancy, business transition, or site closure can be completed. The €2.5M request represents estimated 2027 project investments required to support the currently identified Real Estate portfolio across regions and is based on historical deployment patterns, expected site volumes, infrastructure refresh requirements, and infrastructure components required for new and relocated facilities. Cost estimates are intentionally high-level because detailed site designs become available only after Real Estate projects are formally approved. This demand is categorized under Decommissioning/Replatforming, due to a significant portion of the investment enables retirement and removal of infrastructure assets associated with site closures and consolidations, avoidance of parallel infrastructure operations during relocations, and migration to modern network architectures incorporating NAC, micro-segmentation, and WAN modernization Cost of not doing: Real Estate programs would be unable to execute site openings, closures, and relocations on time; regulatory, security, and operational requirements would not be met; and Philips would face project delays, business disruption, increased risk from legacy infrastructure, and potential duplicate operating costs during site transitions
